turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on in and we'll get the weight and that done. Shoes off if you don't mind.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand. Sorry, the bus was all over the place, I'm a bit flustered.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Not a bother. You're seventy two point four kilos. Blood pressure is one thirty six over eighty four, and the pulse is seventy two.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that ok? I never know with those numbers.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): It's fine for me to record. Doctor will be in now. Were you waiting long?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah a few minutes. I was watching the hurling on the phone, so.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Who was playing?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Kilkenny. I don't know, I only half watched it.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello there, I'm Dr Brennan. Take a seat. What brought you in?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the bloating, doctor, and loose stools. Comes on after milk and ice cream.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. Did you try leaving the dairy off, or are you still having it?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): I did, for a week... well actually it was five days. Then ice cream at my sister's and it all came back. I don't know if those five days helped, doctor.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long has the bloating been going on, before that?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, three months... no, that's not right. It's been since before Christmas, so six months I'd say.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the stools, watery or just soft?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Soft and urgent, two or three goes, not every day, only after the ice cream or cereal with loads of milk. Maybe an hour later. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Your sister, has she the same trouble? You mentioned her there.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No, she's grand. She takes biotin for her hair, that's her thing. And my husband is on metformin for his sugar, but that's him, not me.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ok, not you. What are you taking yourself?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine for the pressure, five milligrams... no, they put it up, ten milligrams in the morning. The cholesterol one at night, atorvastin... atorvastatin, twenty, sorry, forty milligrams. And sugar tablets, gliclazide, eighty milligrams with the breakfast.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any shop stuff, herbs, that kind of thing?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning. A teaspoon, from the health shop. I don't know the name of it, doctor.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. Any blood in the stool at all?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Vomiting? A temperature? Pain apart from the bloating?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No vomiting, no fever. There is a bit of cramp low down when the bloating is bad.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the weight, have you lost any?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I don't think so. Same as I remember, near enough.

[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me think this through. The timing after milk and ice cream makes me wonder about the lactose. But coeliac, the gluten problem, can look the same, bloating and loose stools, and I wouldn't want to miss it.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): So is it the bread? I don't know, doctor.

[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Don't come off the bread yet. If the gluten is out of the diet before the blood test, the test can look normal even if coeliac is there. Keep eating as you usually do until we have the result.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): And what about the milk?

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): You can ease off the milk and the ice cream if that settles the symptoms, that's a separate thing. A diet diary for a couple of weeks would help me, just what you ate and what the bowels did.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I'll try. I'm hopeless at writing things down, but I'll have a go.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Rough notes are grand. I'll book a coeliac screen, bloods, the tTG and the IgA.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I have to starve for it?
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): No, it's not a fasting test. The nurse can take it before you leave.
[SEG0038] person_1 (NURSE): I can, yeah. No bother at all.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand so.

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back in two weeks, we'll go through the result and the diary. If the stools go black, or the pain gets severe, don't sit on it, come in or go to the emergency department.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks... I don't know, doctor, is that long enough?
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): The lab is usually back inside that. Two weeks, yes.
[SEG0043] person_1 (NURSE): Sleeve up whenever you're ready and we'll fill the bottle.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Thanks.

spec.situation: Person with bloating and loose stools after milk and ice cream for months, no weight loss; tried to avoid dairy for a week; blood test for coeliac planned; diet diary asked.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

bad.reason: Husband's condition is mentioned, not family history of the patient.
Doctor says keep eating usual diet until blood test/result; 'gluten-containing' is implied, not explicitly stated.
bad.text: Keep eating usual gluten-containing food until the coeliac blood result (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)

omissions.text: Loose stools occur maybe an hour after dairy exposure.
Doctor advised the coeliac blood test is not a fasting test.
Nurse planned to take the blood sample before the patient leaves.
